content-block-2:
Understanding Advanced Imaging for Your Pet

Advanced imaging options such as CT (computed tomography) and fluoroscopy give our veterinarians a detailed look inside your pet’s body without invasive procedures.

CT uses sophisticated X-ray technology to create highly detailed cross-sectional images, helping to diagnose conditions in organs, bones, and tissues with unmatched accuracy. Fluoroscopy provides live, real-time video of your pet’s internal structures, making it possible to evaluate joint movement, swallowing, and other dynamic functions.

At The Veterinary Internal Medicine Group (VIMG), we collaborate closely with Miami Pet Imaging (MPI), ensuring direct access to state-of-the-art equipment and specialized imaging services. This partnership allows your pet to receive the highest quality imaging possible while maintaining seamless communication between your primary veterinarian and our veterinary internal medicine specialist.

CT and fluoroscopy are vital for diagnosing complex conditions, guiding treatment, and planning the best care for your pet. Our goal is to bring pet advanced imaging services to Miami-Dade and Monroe counties with accuracy, efficiency, and compassion.

What to Expect During Advanced Imaging

When your pet needs advanced imaging in Miami-Dade and Monroe counties, our veterinary professionals focus on making the experience as smooth and stress-free as possible.

We’ll guide you from preparation through to follow-up, so you always know your pet is in capable and caring hands.

Initial Consultation and Assessment

Your visit begins with a thorough assessment by Dr. Armstrong, evaluating your pet’s history and current symptoms.

We discuss the need for advanced imaging, answer your questions, and design the best diagnostic plan. This ensures your pet only receives imaging when truly necessary.

Scheduling and Preparation

Our team coordinates with MPI to schedule imaging at a convenient time and location, often at dedicated pop-up clinics or mobile services throughout greater Miami-Dade and Monroe counties.

You’ll receive clear instructions for preparing your pet, such as fasting if sedation is required or any special considerations based on your pet’s health status.

The Imaging Procedure

On imaging day, we prioritize your pet’s comfort and safety at every step. Most CT scans require sedation so your pet remains still and stress-free, while many fluoroscopy studies can be performed awake depending on the indication.

The imaging itself is non-invasive and usually completed in under an hour. State-of-the-art equipment allows for quick, high-quality results.

Results, Interpretation, and Next Steps

Dr. Armstrong interprets your pet’s images in real time, providing a diagnosis and recommendations during your appointment whenever possible.

We answer your questions immediately and outline next steps, so there is no waiting for off-site reviews or delayed results. This rapid turnaround supports prompt, informed decisions for your pet’s care.
content-block-3:
Why Advanced Imaging is Important for Your Pet

Veterinary advanced imaging in Miami-Dade and Monroe counties is often the key to diagnosing health issues that are otherwise impossible to see with standard X-rays or ultrasound.

CT and fluoroscopy enable early, precise identification of injuries, tumors, spinal or joint disorders, complex internal conditions, and more. These technologies give our team information that directly guides surgical planning, treatment decisions, and ongoing care.

Preventive use of advanced imaging can detect problems at earlier, more treatable stages. By accessing these tools close to home, you give your pet the best shot at a healthier, more comfortable life.

Unmatched Diagnostic Accuracy

CT and fluoroscopy provide high-resolution images that reveal details missed by other imaging methods. This precision helps avoid guesswork in diagnosis.

Personalized Treatment Planning

Our advanced imaging services empower Dr. Armstrong and your primary vet to develop targeted, data-driven treatment strategies, whether for surgery, medical management, or monitoring over time.

Improved Quality of Life

Early and accurate diagnosis means less stress for your pet, fewer unnecessary procedures, and the best possible chance for a positive outcome.

Signs Your Pet May Need Advanced Imaging

Signs your pet may benefit from a veterinary CT scan or fluoroscopy in Miami-Dade and Monroe counties include persistent or unexplained symptoms that don’t respond to standard diagnostics.

  • Chronic or unexplained coughing
  • Difficulty breathing or swallowing
  • Recurrent vomiting or weight loss
  • Lameness, joint pain, or sudden mobility changes
  • Suspected cancer, trauma, or internal masses

If you notice these symptoms, contact The Veterinary Internal Medicine Group right away. Early advanced imaging can be crucial for identifying and treating underlying medical concerns before they become more severe.

How Often Should Your Pet Receive Advanced Imaging?

Advanced imaging services are highly individualized. Most pets only need CT or fluoroscopy when a specific health concern arises, when other tests are inconclusive, or when your veterinarian suspects complex disease.

Frequency depends on:

  • Your pet’s age, breed, and risk factors
  • Chronic health conditions (like cancer monitoring)
  • The need for surgical planning or therapy assessment

For pets with ongoing medical management, our veterinary team will recommend the optimal schedule based on your pet’s unique needs. Reach out for personalized guidance whenever you have questions about whether advanced imaging is appropriate for your dog or cat.
